name: Chondromyxoid Fibroma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Chondromyxoid Fibroma

criteria.description: Presence of lobulated tumor composed of spindle-shaped or stellate cells in a myxoid or chondroid matrix with occasional multinucleated giant cells
Radiographic evidence of a well-defined, eccentric, lytic lesion with sclerotic margins typically in metaphyseal region of long bones
Localized pain and swelling over affected bone, often with a slow progression

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation combined with characteristic radiological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic but may support diagnosis in challenging cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lobulated chondroid-myxoid tumor matrix on histopathology
Well-demarcated eccentric lytic bone lesion with sclerotic rim on imaging
searchTerms: well-defined bone lesion with clear edges
bone area with central bone loss and hard rim
bone lesion with sclerotic border on scan

common.symptomName: Localized bone pain at lesion site
Restricted joint movement adjacent to lesion

rare.symptomName: Neurovascular compromise due to lesion expansion
searchTerms: loss of nerve function due to lesion

laboratory: Typically normal blood tests; no specific laboratory markers
imaging: X-ray: well-defined eccentric lytic lesion with sclerotic margins in metaphysis
MRI: lobulated lesion with heterogeneous signal intensity and peripheral enhancement
CT: cortical thinning and possible expansion without periosteal reaction
other: Histopathology: lobulated tumor with chondroid and myxoid matrix, spindle and stellate cells, multinucleated giant cells

distinguishingFeatures: More aggressive radiologic appearance with cortical destruction and soft tissue mass
Histology shows malignant chondrocytes with atypia and mitoses
Usually central intramedullary lesion without cortical expansion
Histology lacks myxoid matrix and lobulated architecture
Radiology shows expansile lytic lesion without sclerotic rim
Histology dominated by multinucleated giant cells uniformly distributed

redFlags: Severe night pain unrelieved by analgesics
Neurological deficits or neurovascular compromise near lesion
references: Dorfman HD, Czerniak B. Bone Cancers. Cancer. 1995;75(1 Suppl):203-210.
